goal: Replace the provider surface's 'not implemented yet' throws with real, working signing and crypto -- sign, dispatch, signDataItem, batchSignDataItem, encrypt, decrypt, signature, signMessage, privateHash, verifyMessage in apps/extension/entrypoints/background/index.ts and apps/extension/src/handlers/approval.ts -- by wiring arweave-js and @dha-team/arbundles (already the stack's locked choices per core-design.md, arbundles already present for upload signing) into the provider dispatch path. This is foundational: it unblocks every dApp-facing signing capability and the AO-transfer write path AO activity-feed history depends on.
outcome: Every provider method currently throwing 'not implemented yet' performs a real cryptographic operation against the caller's unlocked wallet, resolved via the existing key-session cache (no new password field, same pattern ao-token-send and session-key-persistence already established). Shapes match Wander's confirmed conventions: dispatch returns {id, type?: "BASE"|"BUNDLED"}; signMessage/privateHash accept ArrayBuffer; batchSignDataItem returns a Buffer[]-equivalent; encrypt accepts RsaOaepParams | AesCtrParams | AesCbcParams | AesGcmParams. signature() is documented as ArConnect-deprecated (superseded by sign/signMessage/signDataItem) in the messaging contract's own comments. Every signing action still routes through the existing per-action approval window (decoded preview, verifiable payload hash) -- this task wires the crypto underneath approval.ts's existing approval flow, it does not bypass it. No backward compatibility: the old throwing stubs are replaced outright, not kept behind a flag.

requirements.statement: Signing key resolution reuses the existing key-session.ts unlocked-session cache (getCachedKey(walletId)) exactly as the AR and AO transfer paths already do -- no new password field, no re-deriving key material from a password, consistent with the ratified TransferDraft.walletId wire shape.

core package logic for the new signing/crypto operations has zero chrome.*/window/document dependency (GLEAM-WALLET-RULE-1, unchanged), enforced by the existing ESLint no-restricted-imports rule; only the dispatch wiring in apps/extension touches chrome.* APIs.

Every one of sign, dispatch, signDataItem, batchSignDataItem, encrypt, decrypt, signature, signMessage, privateHash, verifyMessage performs a real operation -- none is left throwing 'not implemented yet', stubbed, or gated behind a flag. No shim or compatibility layer preserves the old throwing behavior for any of them.

dispatch's return shape ({id, type?: "BASE"|"BUNDLED"}), batchSignDataItem's return type (Buffer[]-equivalent), and encrypt's param shape (RsaOaepParams | AesCtrParams | AesCbcParams | AesGcmParams) match Wander's confirmed conventions exactly, since these are verified findings, not open questions.

Every signing operation still routes through the existing per-action approval window (decoded preview, verifiable payload hash) in approval.ts before the cryptographic operation executes -- this task adds real crypto underneath that flow, it never bypasses or weakens it.

Each of sign, dispatch, signDataItem, batchSignDataItem, encrypt, decrypt, signMessage, privateHash, verifyMessage succeeds end-to-end (approval window shown, real crypto performed, real result returned) for an unlocked wallet with a cached signing key -- no throw, no stub.
signature()'s messaging-contract comment documents it as ArConnect-deprecated, superseded by sign/signMessage/signDataItem.

pnpm vitest run provider bridge approval connected-apps content/index background/index passes; pnpm tsc -p packages/messaging --noEmit and pnpm tsc -p packages/core --noEmit pass; pnpm wxt build succeeds with arweave-js/@dha-team/arbundles wired into the provider dispatch path.
